questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The Abacus, one of the earliest known calculating devices, primarily works by
options: using beads on rods to represent and manipulate numbers
storing electronic data on a magnetic disk
processing instructions using a central processing unit
connecting to other devices via a network
questions.explanation: The Abacus is an ancient manual calculating device that uses beads sliding along rods or in grooves to represent numbers and perform arithmetic calculations.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Napier's Bones, an early calculating device, was primarily designed to assist with
options: storing digital photographs
processing text documents
connecting to the internet
multiplication and division calculations
questions.explanation: Napier's Bones, invented by John Napier, consisted of numbered rods used to simplify and speed up multiplication and division calculations.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The Pascaline, an early mechanical calculating device, was invented by
options: John Napier
Ada Lovelace
Blaise Pascal
Charles Babbage
questions.explanation: The Pascaline was a mechanical calculator invented by the French mathematician Blaise Pascal, capable of performing addition and subtraction.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The Analytical Engine, an important precursor to the modern computer, was designed by
options: Bill Gates
Blaise Pascal
Charles Babbage
John Napier
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, a mechanical general-purpose computing device considered a significant conceptual precursor to modern computers, though it was never fully built in his lifetime.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: First generation computers, an early era of computing technology, primarily used which technology for their circuitry?
options: Integrated circuits
Microprocessors
Transistors
Vacuum tubes
questions.explanation: First generation computers (roughly the 1940s-1950s) relied on vacuum tubes for their electronic circuitry, making them large, power-hungry, and prone to frequent failure.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Second generation computers marked a significant advancement by replacing vacuum tubes with
options: Microprocessors
Artificial intelligence chips
Integrated circuits
Transistors
questions.explanation: Second generation computers (roughly the late 1950s-1960s) used transistors instead of vacuum tubes, resulting in smaller, faster, more reliable, and more energy-efficient machines.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Third generation computers are particularly characterised by the introduction of
options: Transistors as the primary new innovation
Integrated circuits
Vacuum tubes
Artificial intelligence
questions.explanation: Third generation computers (roughly the 1960s-1970s) introduced integrated circuits, which combined multiple transistors onto a single chip, further improving speed, size, and reliability.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Fourth generation computers are particularly characterised by the introduction of
options: Vacuum tubes
Transistors as the primary new innovation
Integrated circuits as the primary new innovation
Microprocessors
questions.explanation: Fourth generation computers (from the 1970s onward) introduced the microprocessor, which integrated an entire CPU onto a single chip, enabling the development of personal computers.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Fifth generation computers are generally associated with advancements in
options: artificial intelligence and parallel processing
the initial invention of integrated circuits
the initial invention of the vacuum tube
the initial invention of the transistor
questions.explanation: Fifth generation computing is generally associated with the development of artificial intelligence, natural language processing, and advanced parallel processing capabilities.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A mainframe computer is best described as a
options: a specialised device used exclusively for gaming
small, portable computer designed for individual personal use
large, powerful computer capable of supporting many users and processing vast amounts of data simultaneously
the fastest and most powerful category of computer, used for complex scientific calculations
questions.explanation: Mainframe computers are large-scale systems designed to support numerous simultaneous users and process massive volumes of data, commonly used by large organisations such as banks.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A supercomputer is best described as
options: an outdated computer technology no longer in use
a small, portable computer designed for individual use
the fastest and most powerful category of computer, used for highly complex computational tasks
a computer designed exclusively for basic word processing
questions.explanation: Supercomputers represent the pinnacle of computing power and speed, used for extremely demanding computational tasks such as weather forecasting, scientific simulations, and complex modelling.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A microcomputer (personal computer), as a category of computer, is best described as
options: a large computer supporting hundreds of simultaneous users
a computer that predates the mainframe computer
a small computer designed for individual use, such as a desktop or laptop
the fastest category of computer used for scientific research
questions.explanation: Microcomputers, commonly known as personal computers, are relatively small, affordable computers designed for use by a single individual, such as desktops and laptops.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A minicomputer, as a category of computer, is generally described as
options: a computer used exclusively for supercomputing tasks
the smallest possible computing device
a computer that only existed before the first generation of computers
a mid-sized computer, more powerful than a microcomputer but smaller and less powerful than a mainframe
questions.explanation: Minicomputers occupy a middle ground in computing power and size, being more capable than personal microcomputers but smaller and less powerful than large mainframe systems.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is often referred to as the
options: output device used to display results
input device used to enter data
primary storage device of the computer
'brain' of the computer, responsible for executing instructions
questions.explanation: The CPU is the core component responsible for interpreting and executing instructions, coordinating nearly all computer operations, earning it the common nickname 'the brain of the computer'.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), a component of the CPU, is primarily responsible for
options: controlling input and output devices
managing network connections
storing data permanently
performing arithmetic calculations and logical operations
questions.explanation: The ALU is the part of the CPU that carries out arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction, etc.) and logical operations (comparisons, such as AND/OR/NOT).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The Control Unit (CU), a component of the CPU, is primarily responsible for
options: storing data on a hard disk
connecting to the internet
performing arithmetic calculations
directing and coordinating the operations of the computer's other components
questions.explanation: The Control Unit manages and coordinates the activities of the CPU and other computer components, directing the flow of data and instructions through the system.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Registers, found within the CPU, are best described as
options: external devices used for printing documents
large permanent storage devices for saving files long-term
small, extremely fast storage locations used to hold data temporarily during processing
devices used to connect to a computer network
questions.explanation: Registers are very small but extremely fast storage locations built directly into the CPU, used to hold data and instructions temporarily during immediate processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Random Access Memory (RAM), a type of primary memory, is characterised by being
options: volatile, meaning its contents are lost when the computer is powered off
used exclusively for permanent long-term file storage
non-volatile, retaining data permanently even without power
a type of secondary storage device
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory, meaning any data stored in it is lost once the computer loses power, unlike non-volatile storage such as a hard disk.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Read-Only Memory (ROM), a type of primary memory, is characterised by being
options: non-volatile, retaining its data even when the computer is powered off
a type of secondary storage exclusively
writable and easily modified by regular users during normal use
volatile, losing its data when the computer is powered off
questions.explanation: ROM is non-volatile memory that retains its stored data (typically essential startup instructions) even when the computer is powered off, unlike RAM.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A Hard Disk Drive (HDD), a common secondary storage device, stores data using
options: magnetic storage on spinning disks (platters)
flash memory chips with no moving parts
optical laser technology exclusively
volatile memory chips
questions.explanation: HDDs store data magnetically on rotating platters, using a mechanical read/write head to access the stored information, distinguishing them from solid-state storage technologies.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A Solid State Drive (SSD), a modern secondary storage device, differs from a traditional HDD mainly by
options: being significantly slower than a traditional HDD
storing data only temporarily, losing it when powered off
using flash memory with no moving mechanical parts, generally making it faster and more durable
using magnetic spinning disks exclusively
questions.explanation: SSDs use flash memory chips rather than mechanical spinning disks, generally offering faster data access speeds, improved durability, and quieter operation compared to traditional HDDs.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Optical discs, such as CDs and DVDs, store data using
options: magnetic storage on spinning platters
volatile electronic memory
laser technology to read and write data on a reflective disc surface
flash memory chips
questions.explanation: Optical storage media use laser light to read and, in writable formats, burn data onto the reflective surface of a disc.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A flash drive (USB drive), a portable secondary storage device, stores data using
options: volatile RAM chips only
optical laser technology
solid-state flash memory technology
magnetic spinning disks
questions.explanation: Flash drives use solid-state flash memory chips to store data persistently, offering a compact, portable, and durable storage solution with no moving parts.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The keyboard, mouse, and scanner are all examples of
options: output devices, used to display or present processed data
storage devices, used to save data permanently
input devices, used to enter data or commands into a computer
processing devices, used to execute instructions
questions.explanation: Keyboards, mice, and scanners are classified as input devices because they allow users to enter data, commands, or images into the computer system.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A monitor, printer, and plotter are all examples of
options: input devices, used to enter data into a computer
storage devices, used to save data
output devices, used to present or display processed data to the user
processing devices, used to execute instructions
questions.explanation: Monitors, printers, and plotters are classified as output devices, since they present or produce processed information for the user to view or use, such as on-screen display or printed documents.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A CRT (Cathode Ray Tube) monitor differs from an LCD or LED monitor mainly by being
options: identical in technology to LCD monitors
a type of printer rather than a display device
larger, heavier, and using older vacuum-tube-based display technology
smaller, thinner, and using modern flat-panel display technology
questions.explanation: CRT monitors use older, bulkier vacuum-tube display technology, in contrast to the slim, flat-panel LCD and LED display technologies used in modern monitors.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An impact printer produces printed output by
options: physically striking an inked ribbon against paper
spraying tiny droplets of liquid ink onto paper
fusing toner powder onto paper using heat
using laser technology with no physical contact with the paper
questions.explanation: Impact printers, such as dot-matrix printers, create printed characters by physically striking pins or hammers against an inked ribbon, pressing the ink onto the paper.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A non-impact printer, such as an inkjet or laser printer, produces printed output
options: using only magnetic storage technology
using only mechanical typewriter-style keys
by physically striking an inked ribbon against the paper
without any physical striking mechanism, using methods such as ink spraying or laser/toner fusing
questions.explanation: Non-impact printers, including inkjet and laser printers, produce output without any physical striking mechanism, instead using techniques such as spraying liquid ink or fusing toner with heat.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A plotter, a specialised output device, is primarily used for
options: producing high-quality technical drawings, blueprints, and large-format graphics
capturing scanned images
connecting to a computer network
typing text documents
questions.explanation: Plotters are specialised output devices designed to produce precise vector-based technical drawings, architectural blueprints, and large-format graphics, often using pens or ink.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: System software is best described as software that
options: cannot be run on any modern computer
is designed exclusively for end-user tasks like word processing
manages and controls computer hardware, providing a platform for application software to run
is used exclusively for playing video games
questions.explanation: System software, most notably the operating system, manages the computer's hardware resources and provides the underlying platform on which application software operates.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An operating system's memory management function primarily involves
options: creating spreadsheets for data analysis
printing documents to a connected printer
allocating and managing the computer's memory resources among running programs
designing graphics for presentations
questions.explanation: Memory management is a core operating system function, responsible for efficiently allocating and tracking the use of the computer's memory (RAM) among all currently running programs.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An operating system's file management function primarily involves
options: performing complex mathematical calculations for the user
connecting the computer to a network
organising, storing, retrieving, and naming files and folders on storage devices
creating video game graphics
questions.explanation: File management is a fundamental operating system function that organises how files and folders are created, stored, named, retrieved, and deleted on storage devices.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An operating system's device control function primarily involves
options: designing presentation slides
performing spreadsheet calculations
managing communication between the computer and connected hardware devices, such as printers and keyboards
creating word processing documents
questions.explanation: Device control (or device management) is an operating system function that coordinates communication between the computer's hardware components and the software requesting their services.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a widely used desktop/laptop operating system?
options: Microsoft Excel
Windows
PowerPoint
Microsoft Word
questions.explanation: Windows is a widely used operating system for desktop and laptop computers, distinguishing it from application software like Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, which run on top of an operating system.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: macOS, a widely used operating system, is developed by
options: Apple
Google
IBM
Microsoft
questions.explanation: macOS is the operating system developed by Apple specifically for use on its Macintosh computers.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Linux, a widely used operating system, is particularly notable for being
options: developed and owned exclusively by Microsoft
unable to run on any personal computer
exclusively used on mobile smartphones
open-source, meaning its source code is freely available for modification and distribution
questions.explanation: Linux is a prominent example of open-source software, with its underlying source code freely available for anyone to view, modify, and distribute, unlike many proprietary operating systems.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Android, a widely used operating system, is primarily designed for
options: supercomputers exclusively
large mainframe computers exclusively
mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets
desktop computers exclusively
questions.explanation: Android is a mobile operating system, developed primarily by Google, designed specifically for use on smartphones, tablets, and other mobile devices.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the relationship between an operating system and application software?
options: Application software must be installed before any operating system
Application software controls the operating system directly with no dependency
The operating system manages hardware resources and provides a platform on which application software runs
The operating system and application software are entirely unrelated
questions.explanation: Application software depends on the underlying operating system to manage hardware resources and provide the necessary platform and services for it to function.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following operating system functions is primarily responsible for ensuring multiple programs can run without interfering with each other's use of the processor?
options: Device control exclusively
File management
Process management (process scheduling)
Printing management exclusively
questions.explanation: Process management (including process scheduling) is the operating system function responsible for coordinating how the CPU's processing time is shared among multiple running programs.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Application software is best described as software designed to
options: boot up the computer when it is first switched on
help users perform specific tasks, such as word processing or creating spreadsheets
function only as an operating system
manage and control the computer's hardware resources directly
questions.explanation: Application software is designed to help end-users accomplish specific practical tasks, distinguishing it from system software, which manages the underlying hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A word processor, a common type of application software, is primarily used for
options: creating slideshow presentations
creating, editing, and formatting text documents
performing complex numerical calculations in a grid layout
managing large collections of structured data
questions.explanation: Word processors, such as Microsoft Word, are specifically designed for creating, editing, and formatting text-based documents.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A spreadsheet program, a common type of application software, is primarily used for
options: creating and editing text documents
organising data into rows and columns and performing numerical calculations
designing slideshow presentations
managing complex, structured databases
questions.explanation: Spreadsheet programs, such as Microsoft Excel, organise data into a grid of rows and columns, enabling numerical calculations, data analysis, and the creation of charts.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A Database Management System (DBMS), a common type of application software, is primarily used for
options: performing simple arithmetic calculations only
designing presentation slides
storing, organising, and managing large collections of structured data
creating text documents
questions.explanation: A DBMS is specifically designed to efficiently store, organise, retrieve, and manage large volumes of structured data, such as customer records or inventory information.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Presentation software, a common type of application software, is primarily used for
options: editing digital photographs exclusively
performing complex spreadsheet calculations
creating slideshows to visually communicate information to an audience
managing structured databases
questions.explanation: Presentation software, such as Microsoft PowerPoint, is designed to help users create slide-based presentations to visually communicate information to an audience.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a widely used spreadsheet application?
options: Microsoft Word
Adobe Photoshop
Microsoft PowerPoint
Microsoft Excel
questions.explanation: Microsoft Excel is one of the most widely used spreadsheet applications, distinguishing it from word processors (Word), presentation software (PowerPoint), and image editing software (Photoshop).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of application software, as distinct from system software?
options: Controlling network hardware such as routers exclusively
Booting the computer's operating system
Enabling users to accomplish specific practical tasks
Directly managing the computer's internal hardware components
questions.explanation: The defining purpose of application software is to help users accomplish specific, practical tasks (such as writing documents or managing data), unlike system software, which manages underlying hardware and provides the operating platform.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following would be classified as application software rather than system software?
options: A word processing program
The Android operating system
The Windows operating system
The Linux operating system
questions.explanation: A word processing program is application software designed for a specific user task, distinguishing it from operating systems like Windows, Linux, and Android, which are system software.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Antivirus software, a type of utility software, is primarily designed to
options: detect, prevent, and remove malicious software such as viruses and malware
manage large databases
design presentation slides
create text documents
questions.explanation: Antivirus software specifically scans for, detects, and removes malicious software (malware) such as computer viruses, protecting the system from harmful threats.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A disk defragmenter, a type of utility software, is primarily used to
options: design presentation slides
reorganise fragmented data on a storage disk to improve access speed and efficiency
manage a structured database
create and edit text documents
questions.explanation: Disk defragmentation utilities reorganise fragmented file data scattered across a storage disk into more contiguous locations, generally improving file access speed and overall system performance.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A file compression utility is primarily used to
options: manage a database of customer records
reduce the size of files, making them easier to store or transmit
increase the resolution of digital images
create presentation slideshows
questions.explanation: File compression utilities reduce the storage size of files by encoding data more efficiently, making files easier and faster to store, transfer, or share.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Utility software, as a category, is generally distinguished from application software by its focus on
options: managing only network hardware devices
performing specific maintenance or support tasks that help keep the computer system running efficiently
directly replacing the operating system entirely
helping users perform general creative or productivity tasks like writing or designing
questions.explanation: Utility software focuses on specific system maintenance, optimisation, or support tasks (like antivirus protection or disk defragmentation), rather than the broader productivity or creative tasks handled by typical application software.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of utility software?
options: A word processor
An antivirus program
A presentation program
A spreadsheet program
questions.explanation: An antivirus program is a classic example of utility software, focused on system protection and maintenance, unlike word processors, spreadsheets, and presentation programs, which are application software.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: File compression utilities commonly produce compressed files using formats such as
options: JPEG or PNG exclusively
DOCX or XLSX exclusively
EXE exclusively
ZIP or RAR
questions.explanation: Common file compression formats include ZIP and RAR, which package and compress one or more files into a smaller, more manageable archive.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Data, in the context of computing, is best defined as
options: raw, unprocessed facts and figures with no inherent meaning on their own
a type of network topology
processed facts that have been organised into a meaningful, useful form
a type of computer hardware component
questions.explanation: Data refers to raw, unorganised facts and figures that have not yet been processed or given context, distinguishing it from information.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Information, in the context of computing, is best defined as
options: a type of computer hardware component
a type of software utility
processed data that has been organised into a meaningful and useful form
raw, unprocessed facts with no context
questions.explanation: Information is the result of processing raw data, organising and structuring it so that it becomes meaningful, contextualised, and useful for decision-making.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is a recognised property of good, useful information?
options: Being as vague and general as possible
Being outdated and irrelevant to the current situation
Being deliberately incomplete
Accuracy, relevance, and timeliness
questions.explanation: Good, useful information is generally characterised by properties such as accuracy, relevance to the intended purpose, and timeliness (being available when needed).

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The data processing cycle generally consists of which sequence of stages?
options: Input, processing, output, and storage
Output, then input, then storage, with no processing
Only storage, with no input or output
Only input and output, with no processing stage
questions.explanation: The standard data processing cycle involves inputting raw data, processing it to transform it into useful information, outputting the results, and storing the data/information for future use.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: During the 'input' stage of the data processing cycle, what generally occurs?
options: Data is permanently deleted from the system
Processed information is displayed to the user
Raw data is collected and entered into the computer system
Data is transmitted over a computer network exclusively
questions.explanation: The input stage involves collecting and entering raw data into the computer system, the first step before any processing can occur.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: During the 'processing' stage of the data processing cycle, what generally occurs?
options: Data is physically printed onto paper
Data is transmitted over the internet exclusively
Raw input data is transformed and organised into meaningful information
Data is simply deleted with no further action
questions.explanation: The processing stage is where raw input data is manipulated, calculated, sorted, or otherwise transformed into organised, meaningful information.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: During the 'output' stage of the data processing cycle, what generally occurs?
options: Processed information is presented or displayed to the user
Data is permanently deleted
Data is transformed through calculation
Raw data is initially collected
questions.explanation: The output stage involves presenting the results of processing (the resulting information) to the user, often via a screen, printed document, or other output device.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates the difference between data and information?
options: Data and information are always exactly identical concepts
A list of individual sales figures is data, while a summarised sales report analysing trends is information
Data can never be transformed into information
Information always exists before data is collected
questions.explanation: This example illustrates the key distinction: raw individual figures (data) become meaningful and useful information once processed, organised, and analysed into a report.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In database terminology, a field refers to
options: a programming command used to query data
a complete collection of related records
a single category of data within a record, such as a person's name or age
an entire database containing multiple tables
questions.explanation: A field represents a single, specific category or attribute of data within a record, such as 'Name' or 'Age' in a student database.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In database terminology, a record refers to
options: an entire collection of unrelated databases
a complete set of related fields representing a single entity, such as one student's full details
a single individual piece of data, such as just a name
a type of computer hardware
questions.explanation: A record is a complete collection of related fields that together represent all the relevant data for a single entity, such as all the details for one specific student.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In database terminology, a file (or table) refers to
options: a single field within a record
a collection of related records organised together
a type of computer virus
a single piece of computer hardware
questions.explanation: A file or table in a database consists of a collection of related records grouped together, such as a table containing records for all students in a school.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A primary key, an important database concept, is used to
options: compress files to save storage space
store large amounts of unrelated data
connect a computer to the internet
uniquely identify each record within a database table
questions.explanation: A primary key is a field (or combination of fields) whose value uniquely identifies each individual record within a database table, preventing duplicate or ambiguous entries.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A relational database model organises data using
options: a single, unstructured block of text
multiple related tables, connected through common fields (keys)
purely visual images with no underlying data structure
only a single table with no relationships to other tables
questions.explanation: A relational database model structures data across multiple related tables, linked together through common fields (typically primary and foreign keys), allowing for efficient and flexible data organisation.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: SQL (Structured Query Language) is primarily used for
options: designing graphic images
compressing files to reduce their size
querying, updating, and managing data within a relational database
connecting hardware devices to a network
questions.explanation: SQL is the standard language used to interact with relational databases, allowing users to query, insert, update, delete, and otherwise manage stored data.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is a basic SQL command used to retrieve data from a database?
options: COMPRESS
FORMAT
DELETE ALL
SELECT
questions.explanation: The SQL 'SELECT' command is the fundamental statement used to query and retrieve specific data from one or more database tables.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A foreign key, an important database concept, is used to
options: connect to the internet
compress data files
uniquely identify records within the same single table only
establish a link between two related tables in a relational database
questions.explanation: A foreign key is a field in one table that references the primary key of another table, establishing a relational link between the two tables.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the overall purpose of a Database Management System (DBMS)?
options: To exclusively create text documents
To provide an organised, efficient system for storing, retrieving, and managing structured data
To exclusively design presentation slides
To exclusively connect computers to a network
questions.explanation: A DBMS provides the software infrastructure needed to efficiently store, organise, secure, retrieve, and manage large volumes of structured data.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best represents the correct hierarchical relationship among basic database concepts?
options: Field, then record (a collection of fields), then file/table (a collection of records)
File, then field, then record, in that specific order
Record, then field, then file, in that specific order
There is no hierarchical relationship among these concepts
questions.explanation: The standard hierarchy in database organisation builds from individual fields, which combine to form a record, and multiple related records combine to form a file or table.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Data encryption, an important data security concept, refers to
options: converting data into a coded form to prevent unauthorised access
permanently deleting data from a storage device
printing data onto paper
compressing data to reduce its file size
questions.explanation: Encryption transforms readable data into a coded (ciphered) format, making it unreadable to unauthorised parties who lack the correct decryption key.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A firewall, an important data security tool, primarily functions to
options: compress files to save storage space
physically protect a computer from fire damage
print documents to a connected printer
monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules
questions.explanation: A firewall acts as a security barrier, monitoring and filtering network traffic based on predetermined security rules to prevent unauthorised access to or from a private network.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A data backup, an important data security practice, refers to
options: encrypting data to prevent unauthorised access
permanently deleting old, unnecessary data
compressing files to reduce their size
creating a copy of data that can be used to restore the original in case of loss or damage
questions.explanation: Backing up data involves creating duplicate copies of important data, stored separately, so that the information can be recovered in the event of loss, corruption, or hardware failure.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: User access control, an important data security measure, primarily involves
options: restricting system or data access to authorised users only, often through usernames and passwords
encrypting all network traffic by default
allowing unrestricted access to all data for every user
compressing data files automatically
questions.explanation: User access control mechanisms, such as login credentials and permission settings, restrict access to systems or data to only those users who are properly authorised.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Virus prevention, an important aspect of data security, typically involves
options: disabling all security software entirely
installing and regularly updating antivirus software, alongside cautious computing habits
avoiding all use of computers entirely
sharing passwords freely with untrusted parties
questions.explanation: Effective virus prevention combines the use of up-to-date antivirus software with safe computing practices, such as avoiding suspicious downloads and links.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of encrypting sensitive data before transmitting it over a network?
options: To convert the data into a printed document
To make the file size larger for easier tracking
To permanently delete the data after transmission
To prevent unauthorised parties from being able to read the data if it is intercepted
questions.explanation: Encrypting data before transmission ensures that even if the data is intercepted by an unauthorised party, it remains unreadable and protected without the correct decryption key.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following is a common recommended practice to strengthen user access control on a computer system?
options: Using strong, unique passwords and changing them regularly
Sharing your password with as many people as possible
Using the same simple password for every account
Disabling all password requirements entirely
questions.explanation: Strong, unique passwords, changed periodically, significantly enhance the effectiveness of user access control measures, reducing the risk of unauthorised access.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the difference between a firewall and antivirus software?
options: They are identical tools with no functional difference
Neither tool has any role in data security
A firewall primarily controls network traffic, while antivirus software primarily detects and removes malicious programs already on a device
A firewall detects viruses, while antivirus software controls network traffic
questions.explanation: While both are important security tools, a firewall specifically manages and filters network traffic, whereas antivirus software specifically scans for and removes malicious software already present or attempting to install on a device.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A Local Area Network (LAN) is best described as a network that
options: connects computers within a relatively small, localised geographic area, such as a single building
connects computers across an entire country or continent
is used exclusively for connecting to the internet
exists only as a wireless network with no wired connections possible
questions.explanation: A LAN connects computers and devices within a limited geographic area, such as a single office, building, or campus.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A Wide Area Network (WAN) is best described as a network that
options: exists only within a single building
cannot connect more than two computers together
spans a large geographic area, potentially connecting networks across cities, countries, or continents
is limited exclusively to a single room
questions.explanation: A WAN covers a much larger geographic area than a LAN, often connecting multiple smaller networks across cities, countries, or even continents, with the internet being the largest example of a WAN.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) is best described as a network that
options: spans only a single room
cannot include more than one building
spans a geographic area larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN, such as a city
spans multiple continents
questions.explanation: A MAN typically covers a geographic area intermediate between a LAN and a WAN, such as connecting multiple locations within a single city.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) differs from a standard wired LAN mainly by
options: being limited exclusively to a single computer with no networking capability
being incapable of connecting to the internet
requiring significantly more physical cabling than a standard LAN
using wireless radio signals (such as Wi-Fi) instead of physical cables to connect devices
questions.explanation: A WLAN uses wireless radio signals, most commonly Wi-Fi technology, to connect devices within a local area, eliminating the need for extensive physical cabling.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A bus network topology is characterised by
options: every device being directly connected to every other device
all devices being connected in a closed loop
all devices being connected to a single central cable (the bus)
all devices being connected individually to a central hub
questions.explanation: In a bus topology, all network devices connect to a single shared communication line (the bus), along which data travels to reach its destination.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A star network topology is characterised by
options: all devices being connected individually to a central hub or switch
all devices being connected to a single shared cable
having no central connection point at all
all devices being connected in a closed loop
questions.explanation: In a star topology, each device connects individually to a central hub or switch, which manages and directs all network communication between the connected devices.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A ring network topology is characterised by
options: all devices being connected to a single shared linear cable
devices being connected in a closed loop, with data travelling around the ring
all devices being connected to a single central hub
having no defined connection pattern at all
questions.explanation: In a ring topology, each device connects to exactly two other devices, forming a closed loop (ring) through which data travels sequentially around the network.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A mesh network topology is characterised by
options: all devices being connected only in a single closed loop
having no possibility of redundant connections
all devices being connected to a single shared cable only
each device being directly connected to multiple (or all) other devices in the network
questions.explanation: In a mesh topology, devices have multiple direct connections to other devices, providing redundancy and multiple possible data paths, increasing network reliability.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A router, an important piece of network hardware, primarily functions to
options: scan physical documents into digital format
direct data packets between different networks, such as connecting a home network to the internet
print documents
physically store files long-term
questions.explanation: A router directs data traffic between different networks, most commonly connecting a local home or office network to the wider internet.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A switch, an important piece of network hardware, primarily functions to
options: connect a local network directly to the internet
physically print network diagrams
connect multiple devices within the same local network, directing data to the correct destination device
convert digital signals into analogue signals for telephone lines
questions.explanation: A network switch connects multiple devices within a single local network, intelligently directing incoming data packets to the correct destination device within that network.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A modem, an important piece of network hardware, primarily functions to
options: convert digital data into a form suitable for transmission over telephone or cable lines, and vice versa
print documents
connect multiple devices within a single local network
scan physical documents
questions.explanation: A modem (modulator-demodulator) converts digital computer data into a signal format suitable for transmission over telephone, cable, or similar communication lines, and converts incoming signals back into digital data.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The World Wide Web (WWW) refers to
options: a type of computer hardware component
a system of interlinked hypertext documents and resources accessible via the internet
the entire physical infrastructure of the internet, including all cables and routers
a single specific website
questions.explanation: The World Wide Web is a system of interlinked hypertext documents and multimedia resources, accessed via the internet using web browsers, distinct from the internet's underlying physical infrastructure.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is primarily used for
options: compressing files to reduce their size
transferring web pages and related data between a web server and a browser
transferring files between computers on a local network exclusively
sending and receiving email messages exclusively
questions.explanation: HTTP is the foundational protocol used to transfer web pages and related resources from web servers to users' web browsers.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: HTTPS, a secure variant of HTTP, differs mainly by
options: having no practical difference from HTTP whatsoever
being completely unrelated to web browsing
being used exclusively for sending email
encrypting the data transmitted between the browser and the web server for enhanced security
questions.explanation: HTTPS adds a layer of encryption (via SSL/TLS) to standard HTTP communication, securing the data transmitted between a user's browser and the web server against interception.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is primarily used for
options: compressing files to reduce their size
displaying web pages in a browser
sending emails
transferring files between computers over a network
questions.explanation: FTP is a standard network protocol specifically designed for transferring files between computers over a network, such as uploading files to a web server.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: TCP/IP, a foundational set of internet protocols, primarily governs
options: how files are compressed for storage
how data is broken into packets, transmitted, and reassembled correctly across networks, including the internet
how web pages are visually styled and formatted
how antivirus software detects malware
questions.explanation: TCP/IP is the fundamental suite of protocols governing how data is broken into packets, addressed, transmitted across networks, and correctly reassembled at its destination, forming the basis of internet communication.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Email, an important form of internet communication, allows users to
options: manage a computer's hardware components directly
print physical documents
compress files for storage
send and receive digital messages electronically over a network
questions.explanation: Email enables the electronic sending and receiving of digital messages, along with attachments, between users over the internet or other computer networks.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A web browser is best described as software used to
options: access, retrieve, and display web pages and other resources on the World Wide Web
compress files to reduce their size
print physical documents
manage a computer's internal hardware components
questions.explanation: A web browser (such as Chrome, Firefox, or Safari) is application software specifically designed to access, retrieve, and display web pages and other online resources.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A search engine is best described as a tool used to
options: manage a computer's hardware components
compress files to reduce their size
locate specific information or resources on the World Wide Web based on user-entered queries
send email messages exclusively
questions.explanation: A search engine (such as Google or Bing) helps users locate specific information, websites, or resources on the web by processing user-entered search queries.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) refers to the
options: process of installing antivirus software
process of physically assembling computer hardware components
structured process followed to plan, design, develop, test, and maintain a software system
process of compressing files for storage
questions.explanation: The SDLC describes the structured stages typically followed in developing software systems, including planning, analysis, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A flowchart, a tool used in programming logic, is best described as
options: a type of network topology diagram exclusively
a diagrammatic representation of the steps or logic involved in solving a problem
a type of computer hardware component
a written document describing a company's financial records
questions.explanation: A flowchart uses standardised symbols and connecting arrows to visually represent the sequence of steps and decision points involved in solving a problem or completing a process.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Pseudocode, a tool used in programming logic, is best described as
options: a type of network diagram
an informal, plain-language representation of a program's logic, not tied to any specific programming language syntax
a type of computer hardware component
the actual, executable code written in a specific programming language
questions.explanation: Pseudocode describes a program's logical steps in plain, informal language, allowing programmers to plan out the logic before writing code in a specific, syntactically strict programming language.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An algorithm, an important concept in programming logic, is best described as
options: a step-by-step procedure or set of rules designed to solve a specific problem
a type of network cable
a specific programming language
a type of computer hardware component
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a precise, well-defined sequence of steps or rules designed to solve a particular problem or accomplish a specific task, forming the logical foundation for a computer program.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In programming, a variable is best described as
options: a fixed value that never changes throughout the program
a named storage location used to hold a value that can change during program execution
a type of network protocol
a type of computer hardware component
questions.explanation: A variable is a named storage location within a program that holds a value which can be read, modified, or updated as the program executes.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In programming, a loop is best described as
options: a type of computer hardware component
a structure that executes an instruction exactly once with no repetition
a structure that repeats a set of instructions multiple times until a specified condition is met
a type of network topology
questions.explanation: A loop is a fundamental programming control structure that repeats a block of instructions multiple times, typically continuing until a specified condition is satisfied.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In programming, a conditional statement (such as an 'if' statement) is used to
options: execute different blocks of code depending on whether a specified condition is true or false
permanently store data on a hard disk
always execute the exact same instructions regardless of any condition
connect a computer to a network
questions.explanation: A conditional statement allows a program to make decisions, executing different blocks of code depending on whether a specified logical condition evaluates as true or false.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which of the following best represents the correct general order of the System Development Life Cycle stages?
options: Implementation before any planning or design takes place
Maintenance first, followed by all other stages
Planning/analysis, design, implementation (development), testing, and maintenance
Testing, then planning, then design, then implementation, with no maintenance stage
questions.explanation: The SDLC generally follows a logical sequence: first planning and analysing requirements, then designing the system, implementing (developing) it, testing it thoroughly, and finally maintaining it after deployment.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A key distinction between ENIAC and EDVAC, two pioneering electronic computers of the 1940s, is that EDVAC
options: was built using transistors instead of vacuum tubes
used punched cards exclusively for both input and output
was the first computer to be sold commercially
incorporated the stored-program concept, allowing instructions to be held in memory
questions.explanation: Unlike ENIAC, which had to be rewired to change tasks, EDVAC was designed around the stored-program concept, holding both data and instructions in memory.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: UNIVAC I holds a special place in computing history mainly because it was
options: the first commercially available computer in the United States, delivered to the Census Bureau
the first computer capable of running a graphical operating system
the first computer built entirely from transistors
the first computer to use integrated circuits
questions.explanation: UNIVAC I, delivered in 1951, was the first computer produced commercially in the United States rather than being a one-off research machine.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Charles Babbage's Difference Engine, an early mechanical computing device, was primarily designed to
options: store data magnetically for later retrieval
automatically compute and print mathematical tables using polynomial functions
translate high-level programming instructions into machine code
execute conditional branching instructions from a punched-card program
questions.explanation: The Difference Engine was a mechanical calculator designed to automatically produce reliable mathematical and navigational tables using the method of finite differences.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Unlike the Difference Engine, Babbage's later Analytical Engine is regarded as a true forerunner of the modern computer chiefly because it
options: was the first machine to use vacuum tubes for calculation
could connect to other machines over a telegraph network
was smaller and required less power to operate
included a design for a memory (the 'store') and a processor (the 'mill') that could be programmed with punched cards
questions.explanation: The Analytical Engine's design featured a separate store (memory) and mill (processing unit) controlled by punched cards, mirroring the architecture of modern general-purpose computers.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Ada Lovelace is historically significant in computing because she
options: designed the first commercially sold personal computer
built the first working transistor-based calculator
invented the first electronic vacuum tube
is credited with writing what is considered the first algorithm intended for a machine, the Analytical Engine
questions.explanation: Ada Lovelace wrote detailed notes describing an algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine to compute Bernoulli numbers, earning recognition as an early programmer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The Jacquard Loom, developed in the early 1800s, influenced the development of computing mainly through its use of
options: punched cards to automatically control weaving patterns, an idea later adapted for data input
vacuum tubes to control weaving patterns
an electronic display to preview fabric designs
a magnetic tape system for storing designs
questions.explanation: The Jacquard Loom used interchangeable punched cards to automate complex weaving patterns, and this punched-card idea was later adopted for data input in early computers.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Herman Hollerith's punched-card tabulating machine, first used for the 1890 United States census, is significant because it
options: was powered entirely by vacuum tube circuitry
eliminated the need for any human data entry
was the first machine to use a stored program
demonstrated how punched cards could be used to record and rapidly tabulate large volumes of data electromechanically
questions.explanation: Hollerith's machine used punched cards read electromechanically to drastically speed up the tabulation of census data compared with manual counting.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: One major practical drawback of ENIAC, despite its computing power, was that it
options: could not perform arithmetic operations
relied on thousands of vacuum tubes, making it enormous, power-hungry, and prone to frequent tube failures
used a graphical user interface that confused operators
was too small to house more than a few components
questions.explanation: ENIAC contained roughly 18,000 vacuum tubes, which generated significant heat, consumed enormous power, and failed often, requiring constant maintenance.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Blaise Pascal originally built the Pascaline mechanical calculator to help his father with
options: tax collection calculations
compiling census population data
designing woven textile patterns
astronomical calculations for navigation
questions.explanation: Pascal invented the Pascaline to assist his father, a tax collector, in performing tedious addition and subtraction calculations more quickly and accurately.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Compared with the Abacus, Napier's Bones represented an advance mainly because they
options: required electricity to operate
stored results permanently on punched cards
eliminated the need for any manual calculation entirely
could perform multiplication and division through a set of numbered rods rather than manual bead movement alone
questions.explanation: Napier's Bones used numbered rods to mechanically simplify multiplication and division, going beyond the simple addition and subtraction the Abacus was mainly used for.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which sequence correctly orders these computing milestones from earliest to most recent?
options: Pascaline, Abacus, ENIAC, Analytical Engine
Analytical Engine, Abacus, Pascaline, ENIAC
Abacus, Pascaline, Analytical Engine, ENIAC
ENIAC, Analytical Engine, Pascaline, Abacus
questions.explanation: Historically, the Abacus predates the 17th-century Pascaline, which predates Babbage's 19th-century Analytical Engine, which in turn predates the 1940s ENIAC.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A key reason UNIVAC and ENIAC are both classified as early electronic computers, despite their differences, is that both
options: used mechanical gears as their primary calculating mechanism
processed information using electronic circuitry rather than purely mechanical or electromechanical parts
were designed exclusively for business payroll processing
were portable devices meant for personal home use
questions.explanation: Both ENIAC and UNIVAC relied on electronic components such as vacuum tubes to process data, distinguishing them from earlier mechanical and electromechanical devices.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A digital computer differs fundamentally from an analog computer in that a digital computer
options: processes data represented as discrete binary values (0s and 1s)
cannot be used for scientific measurement
processes data as continuous physical quantities such as voltage or temperature
requires no electrical power to operate
questions.explanation: Digital computers represent and process data using discrete binary digits, whereas analog computers work directly with continuously varying physical quantities.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An analog computer would be most suitable for a task such as
options: measuring and continuously representing a physical quantity such as speed or temperature in a scientific instrument
running a word processing application
storing a company's customer database
processing payroll records for a large company
questions.explanation: Analog computers excel at directly measuring and representing continuously varying physical quantities, such as speed, pressure, or temperature, rather than discrete symbolic data.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A hybrid computer is best described as a machine that
options: can only perform one task at a time with no multitasking
is exclusively used for military applications
uses only mechanical components with no electronic circuitry
combines features of both digital and analog computers, often converting analog signals into digital data for processing
questions.explanation: Hybrid computers combine analog input capabilities, such as reading continuous signals from sensors, with digital processing for accuracy, commonly used in equipment like ICU patient monitors.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A patient-monitoring system in a hospital intensive care unit, which reads continuous vital-sign signals and converts them into digital numeric displays, is a practical example of a
options: hybrid computer
minicomputer
analog-only computer
mainframe computer
questions.explanation: Such a system combines analog sensing of continuous physiological signals with digital processing and display, making it a classic example of a hybrid computer.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The primary distinction between a mainframe computer and a supercomputer lies in the fact that a supercomputer is chiefly optimised for
options: serving many simultaneous users running everyday business transactions
extremely high-speed processing of complex scientific calculations, often using massive parallel processing
running only a single application at a time with no operating system
portability, allowing it to be carried between locations easily
questions.explanation: While mainframes are built for reliable, simultaneous transaction processing for many users, supercomputers are optimised for raw computational speed on complex scientific or simulation tasks, often via massive parallel processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An embedded computer system differs from a general-purpose computer chiefly in that it
options: is designed to perform a specific, dedicated function within a larger device, such as controlling a washing machine or car engine
is only found in supercomputers
always has a full keyboard and monitor attached
can run any operating system or application software installed by the user
questions.explanation: Embedded systems are specialised computers built into larger devices to perform one dedicated task, unlike general-purpose computers that can run a wide variety of software.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which factor most directly determines whether a computer is classified as a microcomputer, minicomputer, mainframe, or supercomputer?
options: The programming language used to develop its software
Whether it has a wireless network card installed
The colour of its casing
Its processing power, physical size, number of simultaneous users it can support, and typical cost
questions.explanation: This size-based classification of computers is primarily based on relative processing power, physical scale, number of users supported, and cost.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A key defining hardware technology that distinguishes third-generation computers from second-generation computers is the
options: widespread adoption of artificial intelligence techniques
replacement of transistors with integrated circuits (ICs) containing many transistors on a single chip
introduction of the microprocessor combining the entire CPU on one chip
replacement of vacuum tubes with transistors
questions.explanation: Third-generation computers moved from discrete transistors to integrated circuits, packing many transistors onto a single silicon chip for greater speed and reliability.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Fifth-generation computers are distinguished from fourth-generation computers mainly by their emphasis on
options: artificial intelligence, natural language processing, and massively parallel processing architectures
the first commercial use of integrated circuits
the first use of transistorised circuitry
the introduction of the microprocessor chip
questions.explanation: While fourth-generation computers introduced the microprocessor, fifth-generation computers are characterised by advances in artificial intelligence, natural language understanding, and parallel processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A computer classified by purpose as a 'special-purpose computer' is one that
options: can run any software application a user chooses to install
is always larger and more powerful than a general-purpose computer
is designed and built to perform only one specific task or a narrow range of related tasks
is used exclusively by government agencies
questions.explanation: Special-purpose computers are built to perform a specific, narrowly defined function, such as controlling traffic lights, unlike general-purpose computers designed for a wide variety of tasks.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A workstation, as a category of computing device, is best described as a
options: high-performance single-user computer typically used for demanding technical tasks such as engineering design or graphics rendering
low-powered device with no processing capability of its own
computer designed to serve as a network's central file server for thousands of users
portable handheld device with a touchscreen only
questions.explanation: A workstation is a powerful, single-user computer with greater processing capability than an ordinary personal computer, often used for specialised technical or scientific work.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In terms of typical processing power, which ordering, from lowest to highest, is generally correct?
options: Mainframe, supercomputer, microcomputer, minicomputer
Supercomputer, mainframe, minicomputer, microcomputer
Minicomputer, microcomputer, supercomputer, mainframe
Microcomputer, minicomputer, mainframe, supercomputer
questions.explanation: In general classification, microcomputers have the least processing power, followed by minicomputers, then mainframes, with supercomputers offering the greatest raw computational power.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A key reason a server used to host a company website would typically be classified differently from an ordinary desktop microcomputer is that the server is
options: always physically smaller than a desktop computer
incapable of running an operating system
optimised to manage network resources and respond to many simultaneous client requests reliably
unable to process any data at all
questions.explanation: Servers are built and configured to reliably manage shared resources and handle many simultaneous requests from client computers on a network, unlike a typical single-user desktop.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Cache memory is best distinguished from main RAM by the fact that cache
options: is used exclusively for permanent long-term file storage
has a larger capacity than RAM but is much slower
is a much smaller, faster memory located closer to the CPU that stores frequently used data and instructions
is non-volatile and retains data even after power is switched off
questions.explanation: Cache memory is a small, very fast memory positioned between the CPU and RAM, holding frequently accessed data and instructions to speed up processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Considering speed, volatility, and typical size together, which statement correctly ranks RAM, ROM, and cache memory?
options: ROM, RAM, and cache all have identical speed and volatility characteristics
RAM is non-volatile, while both ROM and cache lose their contents when power is off
Cache is the fastest but smallest, RAM is slower but larger, and ROM is non-volatile and holds firmware
ROM is faster than cache, and cache is faster than RAM
questions.explanation: Cache is the fastest but smallest memory closest to the CPU, RAM is larger but slower and volatile, while ROM is non-volatile and typically stores firmware instructions.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A memory type is described as 'volatile' if it
options: permanently retains its data even without power
loses all its stored data as soon as electrical power is removed
can only be read from, never written to
is used only for storing the computer's startup firmware
questions.explanation: Volatile memory, such as RAM, requires continuous power to retain its contents and loses all stored data once power is switched off.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory) is distinguished from ordinary PROM mainly because EEPROM
options: can be erased and reprogrammed electrically multiple times without removing it from the computer
can only be programmed once at the factory and never changed again
loses its data whenever the computer is switched off
is used exclusively as a replacement for the hard disk
questions.explanation: EEPROM can be erased and rewritten electrically, often in place, allowing firmware such as BIOS to be updated, unlike basic PROM which can be programmed only once.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In the Von Neumann architecture that underlies most modern computers, a defining principle is that
options: output devices are directly wired to input devices, bypassing the CPU
both program instructions and data are stored together in the same memory
instructions must always be entered manually for every operation
the CPU and memory must be physically located in separate machines
questions.explanation: The Von Neumann architecture stores both data and program instructions in the same memory, allowing the CPU to fetch and execute stored instructions sequentially.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The system bus in a computer, comprising the data bus, address bus, and control bus, primarily functions to
options: convert analog input signals into digital form
physically cool the CPU during heavy processing
store the computer's permanent operating system files
carry electrical signals that transfer data, memory addresses, and control instructions between the CPU and other components
questions.explanation: The system bus is the set of electrical pathways that carries data, addresses, and control signals between the CPU, memory, and other hardware components.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A computer's clock speed, typically measured in gigahertz (GHz), indicates
options: the resolution of the computer's display monitor
the number of processing cycles the CPU can perform per second
the total number of ports available for connecting peripherals
the amount of secondary storage available on the hard disk
questions.explanation: Clock speed measures how many instruction cycles a CPU can execute each second, with a higher GHz value generally indicating faster processing capability.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The most important distinction between primary storage (memory) and secondary storage in a computer system is that primary storage
options: cannot be used to store an operating system
is always non-volatile and retains data indefinitely without power
has a much larger capacity than any secondary storage device
is directly accessible to the CPU for immediate processing, while secondary storage holds data for long-term, non-volatile retention
questions.explanation: Primary storage, such as RAM, is directly and quickly accessible by the CPU during processing, while secondary storage, like a hard disk, provides slower but persistent long-term storage.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A touchscreen on a modern smartphone or tablet is best classified as
options: a pure input device only
a type of secondary storage device
a pure output device only
both an input and output device, since it displays information and also accepts touch-based commands
questions.explanation: A touchscreen serves a dual role, displaying visual output like a monitor while also accepting direct touch input from the user, making it both an input and output device.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An Optical Mark Reader (OMR), commonly used to mark multiple-choice exam sheets, functions by
options: detecting the position of pencil or pen marks made in predefined areas on a form
converting spoken words into digital text
capturing continuous analog video images for storage
printing results directly onto paper without any scanning
questions.explanation: An OMR scans a form and detects the presence of marks in specific positions, commonly used to grade answer sheets on multiple-choice tests.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Print spooling, a function commonly managed by an operating system, primarily helps to
options: increase the physical resolution of a printer's output
permanently delete print jobs after a single use
convert digital documents into audio format
temporarily hold print jobs in a queue on disk so a program does not have to wait for the printer to finish before continuing other tasks
questions.explanation: Spooling stores print jobs in a queue on disk, allowing the CPU and applications to continue other work while the printer processes jobs at its own slower pace.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A serial port transmits data differently from a parallel port in that a serial port
options: can only be used to connect a monitor
requires no cable connection at all
sends one bit at a time, sequentially, along a single communication line
sends multiple bits simultaneously along separate wires
questions.explanation: A serial port transmits data one bit after another over a single line, whereas a parallel port sends multiple bits simultaneously across multiple lines.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Dynamic RAM (DRAM) differs from Static RAM (SRAM) mainly in that DRAM
options: is always faster and more expensive than SRAM
is non-volatile and retains data without power
must be periodically refreshed electrically to retain its stored data, while SRAM does not require refreshing
is used only as permanent firmware storage
questions.explanation: DRAM stores data in capacitors that leak charge over time and must be refreshed regularly, whereas SRAM uses flip-flop circuits that retain data without refreshing as long as power is supplied.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The motherboard's expansion slots primarily allow a computer user to
options: compress files to save storage space
add additional hardware components, such as graphics or sound cards, directly to the system
permanently increase the clock speed of the CPU
convert the operating system from one type to another
questions.explanation: Expansion slots on a motherboard allow users to insert additional cards, such as graphics, sound, or network cards, to extend the computer's capabilities.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A sensor used in a hybrid or embedded computer system, such as a temperature sensor in an air conditioner, primarily serves to
options: translate machine code into a high-level programming language
display processed results to the user in printed form
permanently store the system's operating instructions
detect and capture continuous real-world physical conditions and convert them into signals the system can process
questions.explanation: Sensors act as input devices that detect physical conditions such as temperature or pressure and convert them into signals a computer system can process.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A compiler differs from an interpreter mainly in that a compiler
options: translates the entire source code into machine code (object code) all at once before execution
translates and executes source code line by line as the program runs
is a type of hardware component rather than software
can only be used with low-level assembly language
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the whole source program into machine code in advance, producing an executable file, whereas an interpreter translates and executes instructions one at a time.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: One practical disadvantage of using an interpreter rather than a compiler to run a program is that interpreted programs
options: require no operating system to function
cannot be written in a high-level language
generally run slower because each line must be translated every time it is executed
never produce any runtime errors
