questions.explanation: Because an interpreter translates and executes code line by line every time the program runs, interpreted programs are typically slower than compiled programs.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An assembler, as a type of language translator, is specifically used to convert
options: machine code back into a high-level language such as Python
image files from one format to another
assembly language (using mnemonics) into machine code
high-level language statements directly into a spoken natural language
questions.explanation: An assembler translates low-level assembly language, which uses mnemonic codes, into the binary machine code that a processor can directly execute.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Source code and object code differ in that source code is
options: the binary machine-readable form produced after compilation
only used in interpreted, never compiled, programming languages
the human-readable program written by a programmer in a programming language, before translation
always faster to execute than object code
questions.explanation: Source code is the original, human-readable program text written by a programmer, which is then translated into object (machine) code for the computer to execute.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A device driver is best described as software that
options: allows the operating system to communicate with and control a specific hardware device
protects the computer from viruses and malware
compresses large files to save storage space
manages a company's customer records in a database
questions.explanation: A device driver is specialised system software that enables the operating system to correctly communicate with and control a particular piece of hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Firmware is best distinguished from ordinary application software in that firmware is
options: written exclusively in a high-level scripting language
only used for word processing and spreadsheet tasks
low-level software permanently or semi-permanently embedded in hardware, such as a printer or router, to control its basic operation
always installed by the end user after purchase
questions.explanation: Firmware is specialised software embedded directly into hardware devices to control their basic, low-level functions, unlike general application software installed for user tasks.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Open-source software is best distinguished from proprietary software by the fact that open-source software
options: is always more expensive to purchase
makes its source code publicly available for anyone to view, modify, and redistribute
is only available for mainframe computers
cannot be modified by any user under any circumstance
questions.explanation: Open-source software publishes its source code publicly, allowing users to view, modify, and redistribute it, unlike proprietary software whose source code is kept closed.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Shareware differs from freeware mainly in that shareware
options: is always completely free with no restrictions whatsoever
can never be legally distributed over the internet
must always include its full source code
is typically distributed free initially but expects payment or imposes limitations after a trial period
questions.explanation: Shareware is usually offered free for a trial period or with limited features, with the expectation that users will pay to continue full use, unlike freeware which is free indefinitely.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) or its modern UEFI equivalent primarily functions to
options: manage a company's payroll calculations
translate high-level source code into an executable program
perform initial hardware checks and load the operating system when a computer is switched on
compress and archive user files automatically
questions.explanation: The BIOS/UEFI runs power-on self-tests, initialises hardware, and then locates and loads the operating system during the computer's startup process.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Multitasking, as an operating system capability, refers to the ability to
options: permanently store multiple user accounts on one hard disk
connect several separate computers into a single network
run only one program at a time but switch quickly between them so no delay is noticeable
give the appearance of running multiple programs simultaneously by rapidly switching the CPU's attention between them
questions.explanation: Multitasking allows an operating system to give the appearance of running several programs at once by rapidly switching CPU time between them.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A cold boot differs from a warm boot in that a cold boot
options: restarts the computer using the restart option while it is already powered on
is only possible on mainframe computers
starts the computer from a completely powered-off state, running full hardware checks
only refreshes the currently open application without restarting the system
questions.explanation: A cold boot starts a computer that was fully powered off, requiring the BIOS/UEFI to run complete hardware diagnostic checks before loading the operating system.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A Graphical User Interface (GUI) is distinguished from a Command Line Interface (CLI) mainly because a GUI
options: can only be used on mainframe computers
cannot support a mouse as an input device
requires users to type precise text commands to perform every action
allows users to interact with the system using visual elements such as icons, windows, and menus
questions.explanation: A GUI lets users interact through visual elements like icons, windows, and menus, unlike a CLI, which requires typed text commands.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A disk defragmenter and a disk cleanup utility differ in their primary purpose in that a disk defragmenter
options: reorganises fragmented file data on a disk so related pieces are stored contiguously, improving access speed
deletes unnecessary temporary files to free up storage space
compresses files into a smaller archive format
scans for and removes computer viruses
questions.explanation: A disk defragmenter reorganises scattered file fragments so they are stored contiguously, reducing the time needed for the drive to read the file, unlike disk cleanup which removes unneeded files.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Middleware, in a computing context, is best described as software that
options: is used exclusively for playing multimedia files
physically connects two computers using a network cable
sits between an operating system and application programs, enabling communication and data management across a network
replaces the need for an operating system entirely
questions.explanation: Middleware acts as a bridge between the operating system and applications, often enabling communication, data exchange, and management across distributed or networked systems.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Which classification correctly groups an operating system, a device driver, and a file compression utility together?
options: All three are examples of hardware components
All three are types of secondary storage devices
All three are examples of system software that support the operation of the computer itself
All three are examples of application software
questions.explanation: An operating system, a device driver, and a utility program are all categories of system software that manage and support the computer's hardware and overall operation, rather than performing user tasks directly.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In file organisation, a sequential file structure differs from a direct (random) access file structure mainly because sequential files
options: must be read in order from the beginning to locate a specific record
cannot be stored on magnetic tape or disk
are always faster to search than direct access files for large datasets
allow any record to be accessed directly without reading preceding records
questions.explanation: In a sequential file, records must generally be read one after another from the start until the desired record is found, unlike direct access files where any record can be reached immediately.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An indexed sequential file organisation is designed to combine the benefits of sequential and direct access methods by
options: preventing any record from ever being updated once written
storing all data exclusively in RAM rather than on disk
storing records randomly with no logical order whatsoever
maintaining an index that allows quick direct access to a record's location while still supporting ordered sequential reading
questions.explanation: Indexed sequential file organisation keeps an index of key values pointing to record locations, allowing fast direct access while still permitting efficient sequential processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Batch processing, as a method of data processing, involves
options: using only analog computers to handle numeric data
collecting a group of transactions over a period and processing them together at a scheduled time
processing data only through a direct live connection with no delay whatsoever
processing each transaction immediately as it occurs, one at a time
questions.explanation: Batch processing accumulates transactions over time and processes them together as a single group at a scheduled interval, rather than immediately as each occurs.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Real-time processing is best distinguished from batch processing by the fact that real-time processing
options: requires transactions to be manually grouped before processing can begin
responds to and processes data virtually immediately as it is received, with negligible delay
always takes longer to complete than batch processing
can only be performed on mainframe computers
questions.explanation: Real-time processing handles data immediately as it arrives, producing an almost instantaneous response, unlike batch processing which accumulates data before processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: An airline seat-reservation system, which must instantly confirm or deny a booking as soon as a customer requests it, is a practical example of
options: real-time (online) processing
manual data processing
batch processing
offline processing
questions.explanation: Because the system must respond to booking requests immediately to prevent double-booking, it relies on real-time (online) processing rather than delayed batch processing.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In data transmission, a simplex mode of communication allows data to flow
options: only within a single computer, never between devices
in only one direction, with no possibility of a return signal
in both directions, but only one direction at a time
in both directions simultaneously at all times
questions.explanation: Simplex transmission permits data to travel in only one direction, such as from a computer to a printer, with no return communication path.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A half-duplex transmission mode is best described as one in which data can travel
options: in both directions, but only one direction at any given moment, such as with a walkie-talkie
in both directions fully simultaneously, like a telephone conversation
only between two devices located on different continents
in only one fixed direction permanently
questions.explanation: Half-duplex allows communication in both directions, but only one party can transmit at a time, similar to how a walkie-talkie operates.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Full-duplex transmission, unlike half-duplex, allows
options: no error checking to occur during transmission
data transmission only between devices on the same LAN
both parties to send and receive data simultaneously, as in a typical telephone call
data to flow in only one direction at all times
questions.explanation: Full-duplex communication permits both devices to send and receive data at the same time, unlike half-duplex, which restricts transmission to one direction at a time.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Serial data transmission is generally preferred over parallel transmission for long-distance communication mainly because serial transmission
options: sends all bits at once, making it inherently faster over any distance
is less prone to signal interference and skew over long distances since it uses a single data line
requires far more physical wires, improving reliability over distance
can only be used within a single computer's motherboard
questions.explanation: Serial transmission, sending one bit at a time over a single line, suffers less from signal skew and interference over long distances compared with parallel transmission across multiple wires.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Bandwidth, in the context of data communication, refers to
options: the brand of software used to browse the internet
the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a network connection in a given period of time
the physical length of a network cable
the number of computers connected to a single switch
questions.explanation: Bandwidth measures the maximum data transfer capacity of a communication channel over a given time period, often expressed in bits per second.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Data validation differs from data verification in that validation primarily checks whether data
options: has been encrypted before transmission over a network
has been copied correctly from one location to another without transcription errors
meets predefined rules for accuracy, reasonableness, and completeness before it is accepted
has been backed up to a secondary storage device
questions.explanation: Data validation checks that entered data conforms to acceptable rules, such as being within a valid range or in the correct format, while verification confirms data was copied or entered correctly.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A master file, in data processing terminology, is best described as a file that
options: holds relatively permanent, regularly updated records that represent the current status of key data, such as customer details
is deleted automatically after every processing cycle
can only exist on a supercomputer
contains only temporary transaction records awaiting processing
questions.explanation: A master file stores comparatively permanent records reflecting the current status of important data, such as customer account balances, updated periodically by transaction files.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A parity bit, used in basic error detection during data transmission, functions by
options: adding an extra bit to a group of data bits so the total number of 1-bits is odd or even, helping detect transmission errors
encrypting the entire message so it cannot be intercepted
compressing the data to reduce its overall size
permanently storing a backup copy of the transmitted data
questions.explanation: A parity bit is an extra bit added to make the count of 1-bits in a data unit either even or odd, allowing simple detection of certain transmission errors.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The saying 'Garbage In, Garbage Out' (GIGO) in data processing highlights the principle that
options: the quality of output produced by a system depends directly on the quality and accuracy of the input data supplied
only numeric data can be processed by a computer
all data must be deleted after processing to save storage
computers can automatically correct any inaccurate data they are given
questions.explanation: GIGO emphasises that flawed, inaccurate, or poor-quality input data will inevitably produce flawed or unreliable output, regardless of how sophisticated the processing system is.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In the data processing cycle, the 'storage' stage that follows processing and output is primarily concerned with
options: retaining processed information on a storage medium so it can be retrieved and reused later
permanently deleting data that is no longer immediately needed
converting data into a human-readable printed report only
collecting raw facts and figures from the outside world for the first time
questions.explanation: The storage stage preserves processed information on a suitable medium, allowing it to be retrieved and used again in the future without having to reprocess the original raw data.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In a URL such as https://www.example.com/products, the segment 'https' specifically indicates the
options: internet service provider hosting the website
protocol used to securely transfer data between the browser and the web server
specific file or page being requested on the server
domain name of the website being visited
questions.explanation: The 'https' portion of a URL specifies the protocol, in this case a secure version of HTTP, used to transfer data between the browser and the server.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The Domain Name System (DNS) primarily functions to
options: compress large files before they are downloaded
translate human-readable domain names, such as example.com, into the numeric IP addresses computers use to locate each other
block unauthorised access to a computer network
encrypt all data sent between a browser and a website
questions.explanation: DNS acts like an address book for the internet, translating easy-to-remember domain names into the numeric IP addresses that computers actually use to communicate.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Browser cookies are best described as small pieces of data that
options: permanently damage a computer's operating system
are required for a computer to connect to the internet at all
are stored by a website on a user's device to remember information such as login status or preferences across visits
physically increase a computer's processing speed
questions.explanation: Cookies are small text files that websites store on a user's device to remember information, such as login sessions, preferences, or shopping cart contents, between visits.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Using Boolean search operators such as AND, OR, and NOT in a search engine query primarily helps a user to
options: automatically translate search results into another language
increase the internet connection speed while searching
refine and narrow down search results by specifying required, alternative, or excluded terms
prevent the search engine from tracking the user's activity
questions.explanation: Boolean operators let a user combine or exclude search terms logically, for example requiring both terms with AND or excluding a term with NOT, to produce more relevant results.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Phishing, a common online security threat, is best described as an attempt to
options: legally purchase software licences at a discounted rate
deceive a user, often via fraudulent emails or websites, into revealing sensitive information such as passwords or bank details
increase a website's search engine ranking through legitimate means
physically damage computer hardware using malware
questions.explanation: Phishing involves tricking users, often through fake emails or websites that impersonate legitimate organisations, into disclosing sensitive personal or financial information.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: One reliable way to help identify a phishing email is to check whether it
options: was sent from an address that closely mimics, but does not exactly match, a legitimate organisation's official domain
contains a company logo of any kind
was received during normal business hours
was sent using a well-known email provider such as Gmail or Yahoo
questions.explanation: Phishing emails often use sender addresses or domains that closely resemble but subtly differ from a legitimate organisation's genuine domain, which is a key warning sign.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Netiquette refers to
options: the set of accepted rules of polite and responsible behaviour when communicating online
the hardware standard used for network cables
a type of anti-virus software
the technical protocol used to route data packets across the internet
questions.explanation: Netiquette describes the accepted norms of courteous and responsible conduct expected when communicating and interacting with others online.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Cloud storage services, such as Google Drive or OneDrive, primarily support digital collaboration by allowing
options: documents to be printed automatically without user action
files to be permanently deleted once shared with another user
only a single user to ever access a given file at any time
multiple users in different locations to access, edit, and share the same documents over the internet
questions.explanation: Cloud storage allows files to be stored centrally online so multiple users, regardless of location, can access, edit, and share the same documents collaboratively.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Two-factor authentication improves online account security mainly by
options: requiring only a username with no password at all
removing the need for any password whatsoever
automatically sharing the user's password with trusted contacts
requiring a second, independent form of verification in addition to a password, such as a one-time code sent to a phone
questions.explanation: Two-factor authentication adds an extra verification step, such as a one-time code sent to a mobile device, making it much harder for an attacker to gain access with a password alone.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: In an email message, the key difference between using 'Cc' (carbon copy) and 'Bcc' (blind carbon copy) is that recipients listed under Bcc
options: cannot reply to the email at all
are hidden from other recipients, who cannot see that they also received the message
will receive the email faster than those listed under Cc
will automatically have the email marked as spam
questions.explanation: Recipients placed in the Bcc field remain hidden from all other recipients, whereas everyone can see the addresses listed in the Cc field.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A web browser's cache differs from its browsing history in that the cache
options: is a list of previously visited website addresses arranged by date
permanently records every password a user has ever entered
temporarily stores copies of webpage files, such as images, so pages load faster on repeat visits
is used to encrypt data sent to a website
questions.explanation: A browser cache stores temporary copies of webpage resources like images and scripts locally so that revisited pages load more quickly, unlike browsing history which logs visited addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Video conferencing platforms used for online meetings and digital collaboration primarily rely on which combination of internet capabilities?
options: Offline storage of meeting recordings with no live interaction
One-way simplex transmission of text messages only
Real-time transmission of audio and video data between participants over the internet
Batch file transfer only, with no live audio or video
questions.explanation: Video conferencing depends on real-time, typically full-duplex, transmission of audio and video streams between participants so they can interact live over the internet.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A hyperlink embedded in a webpage functions primarily to
options: automatically download antivirus software
allow a user to click and be taken directly to another webpage, document, or resource
permanently encrypt the current webpage
increase the processing speed of the user's computer
questions.explanation: A hyperlink is a clickable reference that takes the user directly to another webpage, file, or location, enabling easy navigation across the web.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Adjusting privacy settings on a social media account to restrict who can view personal posts is an important online safety practice mainly because it helps to
options: automatically improve the user's internet connection speed
reduce the risk of personal information being accessed and misused by unintended or malicious parties
increase the number of advertisements shown to the user
guarantee that the account can never be hacked
questions.explanation: Restricting who can view personal information reduces the exposure of sensitive details to strangers or malicious actors who might misuse them.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Spam filtering in an email system primarily works to
options: permanently increase the storage capacity of an email inbox
translate emails written in foreign languages
automatically identify and separate unsolicited, often unwanted or malicious, bulk email from a user's main inbox
compress email attachments to reduce their file size
questions.explanation: Spam filters analyse incoming email for characteristics typical of unsolicited bulk or malicious messages and automatically divert them away from the main inbox.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A key distinguishing feature of a computer worm, as opposed to a typical computer virus, is that a worm
options: cannot cause any damage to a computer system
only affects mainframe computers, never personal computers
must attach itself to a host file or program in order to spread
can replicate and spread across a network independently, without needing to attach to a host file
questions.explanation: Unlike a virus, which typically needs to attach to a host program to spread, a worm is a standalone program that can self-replicate and spread across networks on its own.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A Trojan horse, as a type of malicious software, is characterised by
options: disguising itself as legitimate or useful software while secretly performing harmful actions once installed
only targeting network routers and never personal computers
being unable to spread through email attachments
openly announcing itself as harmful software before installation
questions.explanation: A Trojan horse masquerades as legitimate or desirable software to trick users into installing it, while secretly carrying out malicious actions in the background.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Ransomware is a form of malicious software that specifically works by
options: permanently deleting itself immediately after installation with no further effect
automatically updating a computer's antivirus software
improving a computer's processing speed as a reward for installation
encrypting a victim's files and demanding payment before restoring access to them
questions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts a victim's files or locks their system, then demands a ransom payment, often in cryptocurrency, before providing the means to restore access.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: The key difference between ethical hacking and malicious hacking is that ethical hacking is carried out
options: with proper authorisation, to identify and help fix security vulnerabilities
exclusively to steal financial information for personal gain
without the knowledge or permission of the system owner
only by government agencies, never by private individuals
questions.explanation: Ethical hacking is performed with the explicit permission of the system's owner, with the goal of discovering and reporting security weaknesses so they can be fixed.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Software piracy refers to
options: reporting a software bug to its original developer
writing original software code from scratch
the unauthorised copying, distribution, or use of software in violation of its copyright licence
legally purchasing a single licensed copy of software for personal use
questions.explanation: Software piracy involves illegally copying, distributing, or using software without the proper licence or permission from the copyright holder.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Copyright law, as applied to computer software, primarily serves to
options: grant the creator of the software exclusive legal rights over its use, copying, and distribution
prevent any software from ever being sold commercially
guarantee that software can never contain any bugs
require that all software must always be distributed for free
questions.explanation: Copyright law grants the original creator of software exclusive rights to control how it is copied, distributed, and used, protecting it from unauthorised exploitation.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Identity theft, as a form of cybercrime, specifically involves a criminal
options: legally registering a new email account
developing antivirus software for public distribution
unlawfully obtaining and using another person's personal information, such as bank or identification details, typically for financial gain
improving their own computer's security settings
questions.explanation: Identity theft occurs when a criminal illegally acquires and misuses someone else's personal or financial information, usually to commit fraud or gain financially.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Cyberbullying is best described as
options: the use of digital communication technologies to repeatedly harass, threaten, or intimidate another person
a legitimate method of resolving online disputes through mediation
a technique used to encrypt sensitive files
a type of computer hardware fault
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying involves using digital platforms, such as social media or messaging apps, to repeatedly harass, threaten, or intimidate someone.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Data privacy regulations, such as Nigeria's Data Protection Act, are primarily designed to
options: establish legal rules governing how organisations collect, store, and use individuals' personal data responsibly
eliminate the need for computer passwords entirely
prevent organisations from ever collecting any personal data
require all citizens to use the same email provider
questions.explanation: Data protection regulations set legal standards for how organisations must responsibly collect, store, process, and protect individuals' personal information.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: Plagiarism in the context of digital content refers to
options: backing up digital files to prevent data loss
presenting someone else's digital work, text, or ideas as one's own without proper acknowledgement
encrypting a document before sharing it online
properly citing and referencing another person's work in an assignment
questions.explanation: Plagiarism involves using another person's work, ideas, or content without giving proper credit, presenting it dishonestly as one's own original work.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A software developer, as an ICT career professional, is primarily responsible for
options: designing, writing, testing, and maintaining computer programs and applications
managing a company's financial accounts using a spreadsheet
printing and distributing hardware user manuals
physically installing network cables throughout a building
questions.explanation: A software developer's core responsibility is designing, coding, testing, and maintaining computer programs and applications to meet specified requirements.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A network administrator, as an ICT career professional, is primarily responsible for
options: designing artwork for a mobile application's user interface
compiling source code into machine language manually
writing marketing content for a company's website
installing, configuring, monitoring, and maintaining an organisation's computer network infrastructure
questions.explanation: A network administrator manages an organisation's network infrastructure, ensuring it is properly installed, configured, secured, and maintained for reliable operation.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A database administrator (DBA), as an ICT career professional, is primarily responsible for
options: managing the security, performance, integrity, and backup of an organisation's databases
designing physical computer hardware casings
repairing damaged network cables
creating television advertisements for software products
questions.explanation: A database administrator focuses on managing the security, performance, integrity, and reliable backup of an organisation's databases.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: A cybersecurity analyst, as an ICT career professional, is primarily concerned with
options: monitoring systems for security threats and implementing measures to protect an organisation's data and networks from attack
writing user manuals for office furniture
designing print advertisements for computer products
assembling physical computer hardware in a factory
questions.explanation: A cybersecurity analyst's role centres on monitoring for threats, identifying vulnerabilities, and implementing protective measures to defend an organisation's data and systems.

questions.subject: Computer Studies
questions.text: From an ethical standpoint, gaining unauthorised access to another person's computer system, even without causing any visible damage, is generally considered
options: acceptable, as long as no files are altered or deleted
unethical and often illegal, since it violates the owner's right to control access to their own system and data
irrelevant to computer ethics, since only data theft counts as a violation
required practice for all IT professionals
questions.explanation: Unauthorised access to a computer system violates the owner's right to control who may use their system and data, making it unethical and typically illegal regardless of whether damage occurs.
